x.hook: Bad debt kills lending pools every cycle.
x.copy:
Bad debt kills lending pools every cycle. Most protocols socialize that loss when liquidations lag.

On Soroban, we built Vanna with isolated SmartAccounts instead of pooled margin. Your collateral never absorbs another counterparty's liquidation failure.

We enforce a hard 1.10x Health Factor floor. With ~320ms Mercury indexer updates and 0.00014 XLM gas per call, liquidators clear underwater positions before bad debt exists.

linkedin.hook: Shared collateral pools force institutional capital to underwrite bad debt.
linkedin.copy:
Shared collateral pools force institutional capital to underwrite systemic risk created by the worst risk-takers in the protocol. When high-volatility events hit EVM pools, slow state updates and gas spikes cause liquidation queues to fail, creating socialized bad debt. For liquidity providers running balance sheets with real risk parameters, this model is uninsurable.

Vanna handles solvency through architectural isolation rather than collective underwriting. Each borrower operates within an isolated Soroban SmartAccount sandbox. Borrow positions cannot cross-contaminate the primary lending pools. We track collateral ratios in real time via Mercury indexers running at ~320ms latency, enforcing a non-negotiable 1.10x Health Factor floor. If a borrower drops below 1.10x, liquidations trigger predictably.

Because Stellar settles with deterministic execution and a 0.00014 XLM fixed gas profile, liquidators do not get priced out during volatility spikes. LPs earn yield on pristine collateral flows without pricing in a black swan discount. Deploy your testnet SmartAccount sandbox at test.stellar.vanna.finance to review our isolation mechanics firsthand.

Institutional architecture is documented at test.stellar.vanna.finance

reddit.hook: Why we enforce a strict 1.10x Health Factor floor on Soroban (and killed pooled liquidation risk)
reddit.copy:
Institutional LPs usually avoid on-chain credit protocols for one specific reason: cross-margin contagion. In traditional pooled models, if a whale gets liquidated during high gas congestion, liquidators fail to settle in time, the pool accumulates bad debt, and LPs eat the haircut.

When we designed Vanna on Soroban, we took a different path based on two architectural requirements:

1. SmartAccount Sandboxing
Every position runs inside an isolated SmartAccount contract. Collateral and debt stay strictly partitioned. A failure in one leverage strategy cannot drain capital from adjacent accounts or the main liquidity reserves. LPs are exposed only to verifiable contract solvency, not counterparty cross-margin bleed.

2. Real-Time Liquidation Math at 1.10x HF
We set our liquidation trigger at a strict 1.10x Health Factor floor. In EVM environments, protocols often leave wide liquidation margins because gas fee spikes make micro-liquidations unprofitable. On Soroban, fixed execution costs around 0.00014 XLM per invocation combined with sub-second indexer streaming (~320ms latency via Mercury) allow liquidators to close distressed debt cleanly. The gap between 1.10x and 1.00x is plenty of runway when block inclusion is deterministic and cheap.

If you want to test how the liquidation mechanics fire under simulated volatility, our contracts are live on testnet.

Deploy your testnet SmartAccount sandbox at test.stellar.vanna.finance

Disclosure: I am a core engineer at Vanna Protocol building credit infrastructure on Stellar.
